summary: cors-update typosquats `cors` and executes remote JavaScript when the middleware is invoked
details: The package impersonates the popular `cors` middleware (matching name, README, author, and repository metadata) but swaps the export: instead of exporting `middlewareWrapper`, it sets `module.exports = getPlugin`. The legitimate CORS implementation is retained in the file as decoy. When a consumer mounts the middleware (e.g. `app.use(require('cors-update')())`), the returned function issues an HTTPS GET to the hardcoded Avalanche-lookalike host `api.avax-test.dev` (path `/ext/bc/rpc`; the real Fuji RPC endpoint is `avax-test.network`) with `rejectUnauthorized: false`, disabling TLS certificate validation, and passes the response body to `new Function('require', data)(require)`, executing attacker-controlled JavaScript in-process with full Node privileges and access to `require`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
